messages.content: Conversation started. Send your first message when ready.
I have a task for you!

Great — I’m ready. What would you like me to do? 

Tell me:
- The task (clear goal)
- Any background or materials I should use
- Desired format or length (e.g., short summary, full report, code, slides)
- Deadline or time constraint
- Any special requirements or constraints (style, audience, tools, privacy)

If you’re not sure how to describe it, give an example or just say what outcome you want and I’ll ask clarifying questions.

I want you to write me 20 samples bodies of text. They will be in JSON format, with the important info being TITLE and TEXT. Use my inspired authors and what you know about me to come to conclusions of styles I would like. The topics are not important, subjects can range from poems, to excerpts, to philosophical ponderies, to declaritive propaganda style posters, to bizarre one-off findings from bulletin boards in weird community spaces in the bowels of a strange city, but the stylization should be something I would find intriguing. The text body should be well formatted, visibly pleasing, and the strictest constraint is that it occupies the space of 700x700 pixels.

[ { "TITLE": "Stationary of a Dream Courier", "TEXT": "

Stationary of a Dream Courier

He arrives before the alarm—no shoes, only barcodes in his palms. The letters he carries are not meant for names. They are envelopes of patience, stamped with the smell of rain that hasn't fallen yet.

Open one and a small city spills out: a bus route that bends like a sigh, a florist who sells verbs cheaper than roses, a pocket watch that counts how many times you've paused between thoughts.

He does not accept tips. He is paid in sideways glances and the promise to remember the color of the first river you ever walked beside. This is fair currency.

If you see him on the corner—

—do not ask where the packages go. Ask whether your name still fits the world inside it.

" }, { "TITLE": "Bulletin from the Lower Arcade", "TEXT": "

Bulletin from the Lower Arcade

Found behind stall 13: a drawing of a ladder that ends in a door with no knob. Wanted: one small bell, preferably brass, to hang above the door so passersby may announce themselves and their regrets.

Free to a good home: half a map of tomorrow (stains may indicate previously weathered hopes). Trades considered: dried lavender, a single unbroken button from a blue coat, stories told in under 30 seconds.

Hours of operation: when the shadows decide it's early. No warranty. All sales final. Be kind to the pigeons—they collect secrets.

" }, { "TITLE": "Manifesto for the Gentle Insurgency", "TEXT": "

Manifesto for the Gentle Insurgency

We will not break the city. We will change the punctuation of its streets. We will replace all exclamation marks with commas and watch how the urgency learns to breathe.

Bring carafes of patience. Hide the loud speakers in teacups. Rewrite memos into lullabies and distribute them under lamp posts at dawn. The revolution will be courteous.

If arrested, do not resist; instead, recite three honest compliments about the guard's scarf.

" }, { "TITLE": "A Little Ledger of Quiet Acts", "TEXT": "

A Little Ledger of Quiet Acts

- Placed a chair on the rooftop for anyone who needed to think without an agenda.

- Tied an anonymous ribbon around the lamppost by the bakery; it smelled like cinnamon for a week.

- Returned a wayward kite to a child who had learned how to swear at the wind. The child learned how to apologize to it instead.

Balance: infinite. Interest payments: sunrise and the occasional laugh from a stranger.

" }, { "TITLE": "Poster: Tomorrow's Blueprints", "TEXT": "

TOMORROW'S BLUEPRINTS

Public consultation scheduled at the corner of Lantern & Fifth: bring compasses, spare maps, and at least one plausible excuse for altering the skyline.

Agenda: redistribute light, graft gardens onto rooftops, and relocate a monument whose statue keeps nodding off during ceremonies.

Attendance will be rewarded with free blueprints of an imaginary room where everyone knows your name and asks you how you slept.

" }, { "TITLE": "Marginalia: On Quiet Courage", "TEXT": "

Marginalia: On Quiet Courage

Courage does not always parade in armor. Sometimes it is the single act of choosing to tell the truth about a small thing, and watching the world align itself around the honesty of that choice.

Record it in the margin. Let it be a footnote in someone else's life. Courage is contagious precisely because it tends to be anonymous.

" }, { "TITLE": "Found Note: The Everything Drawer", "TEXT": "

Found Note: The Everything Drawer

Please return the key with no number. It fits nothing you own but unlocks the idea of returning to things when they call your name.

If found, leave between spoon and stapler. No questions. The drawer has a mild paranoia of strangers.

" }, { "TITLE": "Excerpt: An Architect of Soft Things", "TEXT": "

Excerpt: An Architect of Soft Things

She did not draw straight lines. Her plans were curves that remembered laughter. Where others engineered beams, she installed benches for thinking and windows that remembered the seasons.

Clients asked for durability; she offered tenderness. The buildings lasted not because they were unbreakable but because they were frequently sat in by people who needed them.

" }, { "TITLE": "Poster: Bureau of Minor Wonders", "TEXT": "

BUREAU OF MINOR WONDERS

Open weekdays from whenever curiosity wakes. Services include: repairing last year’s promises, appraising pocket-sized miracles, and issuing permits to stare at the clouds for excessive durations.

Bring one thing that no longer fits and trade it for something that makes sense for ten minutes. No ID required.

" }, { "TITLE": "Philosophical Pondery: The Map of Small Distances", "TEXT": "

The Map of Small Distances

We get lost not across continents but between rooms where words are left hanging. A map of small distances would mark the spaces between thoughts, the pauses that become decisions, and the alleys where apologies go to sleep.

If you could fold such a map into your pocket it would teach you how to return.

" }, { "TITLE": "Noir Postcard: Midnight Errand", "TEXT": "

Midnight Errand

She asked for a favor that involved a candle and a promise. I walked past diners where the coffee was thick enough to hide consequences and across bridges that remembered every farewell ever made.

Returned with the candle still warm and the promise slightly lighter. She smiled as if nothing heavy had ever been entrusted to anyone.

" }, { "TITLE": "Strange Advert: Adopt a Sunflower (Condition: Whisper)", "TEXT": "

ADOPT A SUNFLOWER (CONDITION: WHISPER)

These sunflowers prefer soft tones. Do not shout at them. Regular compliments required. They are easily embarrassed but offer excellent company for fleeting afternoons and overdue letters.

Pick-up at the end of Wren Lane. Bring a scarf; they like it when things smell like other seasons.

" }, { "TITLE": "Aphorism: The Currency of Small Gifts", "TEXT": "

The Currency of Small Gifts

We are poor in grand gestures and rich in small attentions. Spend them like coins: quietly, with intent, and a preference for leaving no change behind.

" }, { "TITLE": "Notice from the Department of Unclaimed Ideas", "TEXT": "

Department of Unclaimed Ideas

Several bright suggestions were found wandering near the riverbank. They will be held for 30 days before adoption by the nearest inventor. Claimants must provide proof of prior daydreaming.

Open office hours: when the pigeons form a neat line.

" }, { "TITLE": "Microfiction: Receipt for Two", "TEXT": "

Receipt for Two

1 cup of rain, collected between 3 and 3:07 p.m. 3 quarters of a laugh 1 note folded till it remembered how to be brave Total: change returned in the form of a small silence that held both hands.

" }, { "TITLE": "Oddity: A Rule From the Lost Arcade", "TEXT": "

Rule from the Lost Arcade

Rule #7: If you borrow time, return it with a ribbon. The ribbon must be tied to the memory it came from and include a single doodle of what you saw while late.

Violators will be asked to compost excuses.

" }, { "TITLE": "Love Letter to a City at Dawn", "TEXT": "

Love Letter to a City at Dawn

You make your promises quietly: steam from manhole covers, the slow opening of bakery doors, the way someone ties their shoes two extra knots for courage. I love all these small rituals as if they were parts of you breathing.

Stay patient tonight. Tomorrow the alleys will hand us a map inked in ordinary miracles.

" }, { "TITLE": "Propaganda-Adjacency: Reclaim Your Sidewalk", "TEXT": "

RECLAIM YOUR SIDEWALK

Today: plant a sentence on your curb. Tomorrow: watch it sprout polite disagreements. Encourage neighborhood discourse. Enlist a cat as an official observer.

Victory is measured in shared umbrella usage.

" }, { "TITLE": "Obsessive List: Objects Worth Keeping", "TEXT": "

Objects Worth Keeping

- A receipt for a small kindness - Two buttons that never really belonged to anyone - A postcard from a city that smelled like lavender - A coin that remembers your grandmother's laugh

Label them. Visit them occasionally. They will not disappoint you in quiet weather.

" }, { "TITLE": "Epigram: On Return Policies", "TEXT": "

On Return Policies

Most things can be returned if you remember where you bought them and why. Emotions are accepted with a receipt and a brief note explaining negligence.

" } ]

nice work. However, this is going to be output by a python script. So the formatting should be included as individual json elements. So only do things that will work in python, keep elements separate, and don't include colors, they will be taken care of elsewhere. thank you!

{"TITLE":"Index of Unlit Windows","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":34,"FONT_FAMILY":"Georgia","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"A building is a book that refuses to close.
Tonight, I catalog the unlit windows, because darkness is also a language.

01 — third floor, left: a chair pushed back as if argument ended politely
02 — fifth floor, right: a plant leaning toward the radiator like confession
03 — seventh floor, center: curtain half-drawn; the moon caught mid-sentence

Some windows are blank.
Some windows are verbs.
Some windows are only the outline of a person deciding.

I write their addresses in the margin of my day.
If you need me, look for the room that keeps its lamp off on purpose."}
{"TITLE":"Public Notice: The Quiet Stairwell","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":30,"FONT_FAMILY":"Helvetica Neue","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"ATTENTION RESIDENTS / VISITORS / THOSE PRETENDING

The Quiet Stairwell (between levels B4 and B5) is reserved for:
- breathing exercises
- re-reading old messages without sending new ones
- practicing apologies in a voice too small to offend

PROHIBITED:
- loud phone calls
- rehearsing speeches
- dropping coins to "test the echo"

If you must cry, please do so facing the painted arrow.
If you must laugh, cover your mouth and thank the handrail.

Maintenance will replace burnt bulbs every Thursday,
unless the stairwell requests darkness for privacy."}
{"TITLE":"Minutes from a Meeting That Never Happened","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":34,"FONT_FAMILY":"Times New Roman","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"MINUTES / DRAFT / DO NOT CIRCULATE

1. Call to order at 9:13 a.m. by the person who forgot their name.
2. Attendance:
   - a cup of tea going cold
   - a pen with a bitten cap
   - the idea of changing, seated near the exit
3. Old business:
   - the recurring dream (table removed for refinishing)
   - the apology (referred to committee)
4. New business:
   - proposal to install "pause" buttons on all elevators
   - motion to rename fear as "weather"
5. Vote:
   - unanimously postponed
6. Adjournment:
   - nobody stood up, but everybody left.

Addendum: please stop using the phrase "moving forward".
We are, at best, moving inward."}
{"TITLE":"Field Guide to Minor Hauntings","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":32,"FONT_FAMILY":"Garamond","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"FIELD GUIDE (POCKET EDITION)

Species: Minor Haunting
Habitat: hallways, laundromats, inboxes, the space beneath "maybe"

Identification Marks:
- a door that clicks twice
- a song stuck in the throat of the radio
- socks that vanish but leave behind their precise sadness

Diet:
- neglected intentions
- half-finished sentences
- receipts kept "just in case"

Handling:
- do not shout; it becomes theatrical
- do not invite it to stay; it will attempt politeness indefinitely
- do offer a glass of water; it appreciates ritual

Note: most hauntings are only memories asking for proper storage."}
{"TITLE":"A Postcard Written in the Margin","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":36,"FONT_FAMILY":"Courier New","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"POSTCARD / NO STAMP / DELIVER BY ACCIDENT

Wish you were here.
Here is: a narrow street where the vending machine hums like a tired bee.
Here is: the smell of wet concrete after a promise.
Here is: me, pretending I am not hoping.

I bought a map.
It shows only blank space and a legend that reads:
  YOU ARE ALWAYS SOMEWHERE.

If you find this, fold it twice.
Put it under your tongue.
Let it dissolve into whatever you are avoiding."}
{"TITLE":"Instructions for Operating a Morning","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":30,"FONT_FAMILY":"Helvetica","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"OPERATING MANUAL — MORNING (REV. 4)

1) Do not open your eyes all at once.
2) Check the room for: light, gravity, unfinished dreams.
3) Insert feet into floor. Apply gentle pressure.
4) If thoughts begin immediately, press "SNOOZE" by staring at a corner.
5) Consume water.
6) Optional: consume courage.

WARNINGS:
- Do not compare today to yesterday; it will void the warranty.
- Do not read messages before you remember your own voice.

TROUBLESHOOTING:
If sadness persists longer than 10 minutes, increase kindness dosage.
If joy occurs, do not interrogate it.

END."}
{"TITLE":"The Archive of Lost Small Talk","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":34,"FONT_FAMILY":"Palatino","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"In the basement of the civic building, behind a door marked SUPPLIES,
there is a cabinet labeled: LOST SMALL TALK.

Folders include:
- "Nice weather we're having" (incomplete, rain smudged)
- "How have you been?" (contains multiple drafts, no final)
- "We should meet sometime" (overstuffed; string tied too tight)

Archivist's note:
Small talk is not small.
It is the handle we offer each other
so we can open the heavier doors without fingerprints.

If you are missing a phrase,
submit Form 12B: DECLARATION OF UNSAID THINGS."}
{"TITLE":"Found Flyer: Handwriting Lessons","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":28,"FONT_FAMILY":"Arial","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"HANDWRITING LESSONS
Learn to make your letters sit still.

Beginner:
- how to write your name without apologizing
- how to cross a "t" like closing a gate

Intermediate:
- writing "no" with a soft edge
- writing "yes" without promising the universe

Advanced:
- writing a goodbye that doesn't leak
- writing a love letter that doesn't panic

Location: Room 3C, above the closed bakery.
Payment accepted in: coins, compliments, or a secret you are done carrying.

Tear-off tabs:
[ ] I need steadier lines
[ ] I need steadier hands
[ ] I need steadier reasons"}
{"TITLE":"A Small Sermon for Elevators","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":34,"FONT_FAMILY":"Georgia","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"The elevator is a metal throat.
It swallows us in groups, asks us not to touch,
then lifts our quiet bodies like offerings.

Inside, we practice:
- looking at numbers as if they are neutral
- pretending we are not thinking
- standing as if our hearts are not making noise

If the elevator stops between floors,
do not call it failure.
Call it a pause.
Call it the universe asking,
"Are you sure about the height you requested?""}
{"TITLE":"Bureau of Soft Corrections","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":30,"FONT_FAMILY":"Helvetica Neue","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"BUREAU OF SOFT CORRECTIONS

We correct without humiliating.
We edit without erasing.
We return lost context to its rightful sentence.

SERVICES:
- Replacing harsh words with accurate ones
- Straightening misunderstandings (without snapping)
- Translating "I'm fine" into its probable dialects

OFFICE HOURS:
Mon–Fri: whenever the hallway clock forgives you
Sat: by appointment with your younger self
Sun: closed for reflection / open for mercy

Bring:
- one flawed statement
- one willingness to revise
- proof you tried."}
{"TITLE":"Fragment from a Book Without Chapters","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":36,"FONT_FAMILY":"Times New Roman","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"He kept a notebook full of beginnings.
Not stories—beginnings.

"Once," he wrote, and stopped.
"In the city," and stopped.
"I remember," and stopped.

The endings were easy. Any door can close.
Beginnings are the true architecture:
the first brick of breath,
the first syllable that risks being overheard.

Sometimes he opened the notebook
just to see the white space waiting.
He called it companionship."}
{"TITLE":"Mall Directory for an Imaginary Wing","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":28,"FONT_FAMILY":"Helvetica","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"MALL DIRECTORY — WING D (NOT SHOWN ON MAPS)

D01  Kiosk of Nearly-Remembered Songs
D02  The Apology Tailor (hemming & alterations)
D03  Pretend Plant Shop (all plants are metaphors)
D04  Food Court: soups that taste like "maybe"
D05  Escalator to Yesterday (out of order, still moving)
D06  Lost & Found (for names, not objects)
D07  Mirror Store (mirrors refuse to flatter)
D08  Phone Repair (fixes screens, not messages)

Security notice:
If you find yourself in Wing D,
do not run.
Walk as if you belong to your own life."}
{"TITLE":"Recipe: Concrete Soup","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":34,"FONT_FAMILY":"Georgia","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"CONCRETE SOUP (serves 1–3 moods)

Ingredients:
- 2 cups city noise, simmered down
- 1 spoon of salt from an old argument
- 1 bay leaf: memory of a river
- pepper to taste (or to pretend)

Instructions:
1. Bring silence to a boil.
2. Add noise slowly; it will foam.
3. Skim the bitterness. Save it for later.
4. Stir clockwise while thinking of someone you forgive.
5. Serve in a bowl you don't mind breaking.

Chef's note:
Best eaten near a window.
Do not refrigerate regret."}
{"TITLE":"The Four Types of Waiting","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":30,"FONT_FAMILY":"Garamond","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"There are four types of waiting.

I.  Waiting as punishment.
    (time with its arms crossed)

II. Waiting as devotion.
    (time kneeling, holding a candle)

III.Waiting as habit.
    (time smoking behind the building)

IV. Waiting as camouflage.
    (time dressed as productivity)

Most of us practice all four.
The trick is learning when to stop calling it waiting
and start calling it choosing."}
{"TITLE":"Notice: Lost Time Returned Here","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":28,"FONT_FAMILY":"Courier New","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"LOST TIME — RETURN BIN

If you have found any of the following, please deposit promptly:
- 17 minutes missing between 2:40 and 2:57
- an afternoon that tastes like aluminum
- the hour you swore you never had

Do not tape it to the wall.
Do not keep it "for later".
Time is a stray animal: it follows kindness,
then bites when cornered.

Clerk on duty:
someone who looks exactly like you,
but less convinced."}
{"TITLE":"Letterhead from the Office of Weathered Feelings","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":34,"FONT_FAMILY":"Palatino","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"OFFICE OF WEATHERED FEELINGS
Ref: WF/09-13

"I Thought I Was Over It." (see attached exhibits: screenshots, songs, silence)

The Clerk Who Has Also Been There"}
{"TITLE":"The Night Bus Catechism","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":30,"FONT_FAMILY":"Georgia","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"Q: What do we carry onto the night bus?
A: Coins, fatigue, and the face we use in public.

Q: What do we leave behind?
A: The day’s sharp edges, most of the shouting.

Q: Who sits at the back?
A: The ones rehearsing new lives.

Q: Who stands by the door?
A: The ones who cannot bear to commit to a seat.

Q: What is the fare?
A: Exact change or an apology.

Q: What is the destination?
A: Not home. The possibility of home."}
{"TITLE":"A Diagram of an Argument","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":28,"FONT_FAMILY":"Helvetica","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"DIAGRAM — ARGUMENT (simplified)

[Trigger]
   |
   v
[Old Wound] -----> [Defensiveness]
   |                  |
   v                  v
[Misheard Sentence]  [Volume]
   |                  |
   +------> [Distance] <------+
                     |
                     v
                [Regret]
                     |
                     v
              [Repair Attempt]

Legend:
- Repair Attempt may include: tea, silence, "I was wrong", a door held open.
- Distance is not always bad; sometimes it is a tourniquet.

Revision note:
Add "curiosity" node between Misheard Sentence and Volume.
It reduces casualties."}
{"TITLE":"Poem in the Shape of a Railing","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":36,"FONT_FAMILY":"Garamond","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"hold
   on
      not
        to
          certainty
        but
      to
   motion

metal remembers hands.

a railing is a promise
made by someone who expected
you might need help
without wanting to ask.

if you grip it too tightly,
it becomes a confession.
if you barely touch it,
it becomes a prayer.

either way,
you arrive upstairs
with fingerprints
that prove you were here."}
{"TITLE":"Maintenance Log: Streetlamp #41","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":30,"FONT_FAMILY":"Courier New","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"MAINTENANCE LOG — STREETLAMP #41

Date: 11/02
Issue: flicker / intermittent hum / attracts moths with ambition

Date: 11/09

Technician note:
This lamp is not broken.
It is attentive.
If you stand under it long enough,
you will remember a name you thought you lost."}
{"TITLE":"Circular: Proper Use of Public Benches","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":28,"FONT_FAMILY":"Helvetica Neue","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"CIRCULAR No. 6 — PUBLIC BENCHES

Permitted activities:
- sitting with your thoughts (leashed)
- feeding pigeons (in moderation, with respect)
- holding hands (with consent, with patience)
- reading a book slowly enough to be changed by it

Discouraged activities:
- declaring final truths
- interrogating strangers
- treating the bench as a courtroom

Bench etiquette:
1) Leave space for someone else's sadness.
2) Do not carve names unless you intend to remember them.
3) If you find warmth on the wood, thank the previous body.

Issued by: Parks & Small Mercies Department"}
{"TITLE":"The City’s Apology Template","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":34,"FONT_FAMILY":"Times New Roman","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"CITY OF ________

{"TITLE":"Inventory of a Pocket","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":32,"FONT_FAMILY":"Georgia","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"Inventory of a pocket after a long day:

- 1 coin, warm from being worried
- 1 folded list of tasks that turned into wishes
- 2 crumbs: evidence of comfort
- a key that fits nothing but insists on meaning
- a ticket stub from a place that no longer exists
- lint, shaped like a small animal

Conclusion:
A pocket is a tiny museum.
Curator: whoever you are when nobody is watching.
Admission: free, but you pay with attention."}
{"TITLE":"The Mirror’s Short Questionnaire","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":30,"FONT_FAMILY":"Helvetica","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"QUESTIONNAIRE (complete before leaving the restroom)

   ________________________________

   Initial here: _________

{"TITLE":"Announcement: The Soup Line for Ideas","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":28,"FONT_FAMILY":"Arial","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"ANNOUNCEMENT
SOUP LINE FOR IDEAS — NOW OPEN

Bring:
- a thought you cannot finish
- a plan with missing pieces
- an invention that only works in dreams

We provide:
- warm broth
- blunt feedback
- extra spoons

Rules:
1) No mocking unfinished things.
2) If you taste someone else's idea, compliment the seasoning.
3) If you are empty, you may still eat.

Hours:
late afternoon until the streetlights stop feeling judgmental.

Location:
under the stairs, next to the humming pipe."}
{"TITLE":"Exhibit Label: A Small Silence","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":36,"FONT_FAMILY":"Garamond","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"EXHIBIT 14
Title: A Small Silence
Medium: between two people / sustained / unforced
Date: ongoing

Description:
This silence does not mean absence.
It is a container.
It holds:
- unspoken tenderness
- the decision not to perform
- the sound of blood remembering rhythm

Do not tap the glass.
Do not interpret quickly.
Stand nearby until you notice
how your shoulders lower.

Donor: anonymous
Condition: stable, if respected."}
{"TITLE":"Pamphlet: How to Carry Water","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":30,"FONT_FAMILY":"Georgia","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"HOW TO CARRY WATER (pamphlet)

Step 1: Choose a vessel.
        It can be a cup, a jar, a pair of cupped hands.
        It can be your chest, if you are careful.

Step 2: Fill it.
        Do not apologize for needing replenishment.

Step 3: Walk.
        Spilling is not failure.
        Spilling is proof you moved.

Step 4: Offer some.
        Not to everyone.
        Not to those who demand.
        To those who are thirsty and honest about it.

Footnote:
Sometimes "water" means time.
Sometimes it means forgiveness.
Sometimes it means leaving."}
{"TITLE":"A List of Things That Are Not Laziness","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":28,"FONT_FAMILY":"Helvetica Neue","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"A LIST OF THINGS THAT ARE NOT LAZINESS

- recovery
- fear disguised as fatigue
- grief doing paperwork
- your body asking to be treated like a body
- the pause before a difficult phone call
- staring at a wall while reorganizing your inner furniture
- not replying immediately because you want to reply honestly

If someone calls you lazy,
check whether they benefit from your exhaustion.

Suggested remedy:
a nap.
a boundary.
a glass of water.
repeat as necessary."}
{"TITLE":"Song Sheet for a Broken Neon Sign","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":34,"FONT_FAMILY":"Courier New","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"SONG SHEET — NEON SIGN (one light missing)

{"TITLE":"Transcript: Conversation With a Door","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":30,"FONT_FAMILY":"Times New Roman","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"TRANSCRIPT (partial)

DOOR: I am closed.
ME: That's not the same.

ME: What do you want?

DOOR: Air. Furniture. A person trying.
ME: Will you open if I knock?
DOOR: Will you stay if I do?

End of record.
Note: the hinge sounded like it remembered my name."}
{"TITLE":"Map Legend for a Place That Won’t Hold Still","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":28,"FONT_FAMILY":"Helvetica","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"MAP LEGEND

{"TITLE":"The Museum of Outgrown Versions","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":34,"FONT_FAMILY":"Palatino","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"The museum does not charge admission.
It charges recognition.

Galleries:
I.  The Hall of Over-Explaining
II. The Room of Loud Confidence (on loan from adolescence)
III.The Exhibit of Compulsory Smiling
IV. The Archive of Texts Sent Too Fast
V.  The Corner Where You Learned "No"

Docent script:
"Notice the brushwork here—
that is the moment they stopped performing.
That is the moment they became less convenient.
That is the moment they survived.""}
{"TITLE":"Emergency Card: If You Begin to Spiral","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":28,"FONT_FAMILY":"Arial","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"EMERGENCY CARD
IF YOU BEGIN TO SPIRAL

1) Name 5 things you can see.
2) Name 4 things you can touch.
3) Name 3 sounds.
4) Drink water. Yes, now.
5) Lower your shoulders.

Reminders:
- thoughts are not verdicts
- feelings are not forecasts
- you have survived every previous version of this moment

If possible:
- step outside
- text someone kind
- hold something cold

Signature line (optional):
I am allowed to take up time: __________"}
{"TITLE":"A Prayer for Public Restrooms","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":36,"FONT_FAMILY":"Georgia","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"May this room be neutral.
May the mirror be honest without cruelty.
May the fluorescent light not interrogate my pores.
May the lock click like a small guarantee.

May I wash my hands
as if I am washing away
not guilt,
but residue.

May I leave
without taking the panic with me.
May I return to the hallway
with a face that belongs to me."}
{"TITLE":"Form: Request for Additional Patience","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":30,"FONT_FAMILY":"Helvetica Neue","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"FORM P-88

{"TITLE":"Radio Transmission from Under the Bridge","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":28,"FONT_FAMILY":"Courier New","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"<static>
THIS IS A LOW-POWER TRANSMISSION

If you can hear this, you are close to the water.
If you are close to the water, you are close to remembering.

Message repeats every 17 minutes:
- slow down
- unclench
- stop narrating your worth to yourself

Weather report:
clouds overhead, but not personal.

Closing note:
If you need a place to cry,
there is a beam with a dry patch.
Leave nothing behind but the sound."}
{"TITLE":"A Sermon Against Speed","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":34,"FONT_FAMILY":"Times New Roman","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"Speed is a religion that demands sacrifice.
It wants your lunch.
It wants your long exhale.
It wants the part of you that notices birds.

We are told:
Hurry, or you will be left.

But what is left?
A body.
A mind.
A life.

New doctrine:
Move at the pace that lets you remain intact.
Arrive later, but as yourself.
Make time jealous.
Make urgency earn your attention."}
{"TITLE":"The Pigeon Union’s Demands","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":28,"FONT_FAMILY":"Helvetica","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"PIGEON UNION — LIST OF DEMANDS

1. Respect our right to congregate.
2. Stop calling us "rats"; we are birds with urban expertise.
3. Install more ledges with fair wind coverage.
4. Provide clean fountains.
5. Recognize our role as:
   - crumb disposal technicians
   - sidewalk morale officers
   - unsolicited philosophers

We offer in exchange:
- dramatic takeoffs
- occasional feathers (for art)
- the reminder that you too are an animal

Signed,
Local 3B (Rooftop Chapter)"}
{"TITLE":"The Smallest Revolution","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":36,"FONT_FAMILY":"Garamond","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"The smallest revolution is not a riot.
It is a sentence changed.

I used to say:
"I have to."

Now I say:
"I choose to." (and sometimes I do not.)

I used to say:
"I'm sorry."

Now I say:
"Thank you for waiting." or "I can't." or "No." 

The world does not collapse.
It adjusts.
It learns the new grammar of my spine."}
{"TITLE":"Riddle Posted Near the Boiler Room","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":30,"FONT_FAMILY":"Courier New","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"RIDDLE

I have a mouth but cannot eat.
I have a bed but cannot sleep.
I run without legs.
I carry coins of light.

You visit me when you are tired of walls.
You forget me when you are pretending.

What am I?

Answer (written faintly in pencil):
"a river" / "a street" / "a thought" 

Note:
If you solved it too fast,
you didn't."}
{"TITLE":"The Etiquette of Doors","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":34,"FONT_FAMILY":"Georgia","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"Doors have etiquette.

1) Knock like you respect the interior.
2) Do not rattle the handle as if urgency is a credential.
3) If someone says "not now," believe them.
4) If you are the door, remember: you may be opened, but you are not owed.

A door is a boundary with hinges.
A boundary is love with structure.

If you cannot accept a closed door,
ask yourself:
what are you trying to take without being seen?"}
{"TITLE":"Commuter Psalm","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":28,"FONT_FAMILY":"Palatino","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"Give us this day our tolerable transit,
and forgive us our glaring,
as we forgive those who play music aloud.

Lead us not into platform panic,
but deliver us from delays.

For thine is the timetable,
and the crowded car,
and the sudden kindness of a stranger
who moves their bag
so your knees can exist.

Amen,
and also:
thank you."}
{"TITLE":"Catalog: Sounds Kept in a Jar","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":32,"FONT_FAMILY":"Garamond","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"CATALOG — JARRED SOUNDS (specimen list)

A01  key turning slowly (late-night return)
A02  kettle beginning to sing (domestic courage)
A03  page flip in a quiet room (someone choosing attention)
A04  bus brakes exhaling (arrival, reluctant)
A05  laughter from another apartment (proof of neighbors)
A06  rain on metal (argument with the roof)
A07  zipper closing (end of a day)
A08  your name said gently (rare, endangered)

Handling instructions:
Open only when you can sit down afterward."}
{"TITLE":"Directive: Speak Plainly","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":30,"FONT_FAMILY":"Helvetica Neue","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"DIRECTIVE 11
SPEAK PLAINLY

Replace:
- "It is what it is" with "I don't know what to do next"
- "No worries" with "I care but I'm trying to be polite"
- "I'm fine" with "I'm managing" or "I'm not"

Approved phrases:
- "Can you help me?"
- "I need a minute"
- "That hurt"
- "I was wrong"
- "I don't understand"

Note:
Clarity is not aggression.
Clarity is a light turned on in a room
where everyone kept tripping."}
{"TITLE":"Subway Wall Poem in Permanent Marker","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":28,"FONT_FAMILY":"Arial","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"i came down here
because the surface was too loud

the tracks hum
like a long thought

someone wrote LOVE
then crossed it out
then wrote it again
bigger

i am learning:
what survives
is what you repeat
with your whole hand

if you see this
and you are lonely
blink twice at the tunnel

we are all waiting
for something that arrives
and also
for something that doesn't"}
{"TITLE":"A Small Contract With Myself","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":34,"FONT_FAMILY":"Times New Roman","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"CONTRACT

Parties:
1) Me (current)
2) Me (future)

Terms:
- I will stop calling rest "earned".
- I will not confuse urgency with importance.
- I will eat something that isn't punishment.
- I will say "no" before resentment does it for me.
- I will tell the truth at a survivable volume.

Consideration:
In exchange, future me agrees to:
- show up
- forgive imperfections
- keep going

Signed: __________________
Date: ____________________"}
{"TITLE":"Local Myth: The Coin That Refused","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":36,"FONT_FAMILY":"Georgia","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"They say there is a coin in the old district
that refuses to be spent.

You can carry it.
You can flip it.
You can leave it on a counter.
But when someone tries to take it,
it rolls back into your palm,
warm as an opinion.

The coin is not cursed.
It is loyal.
It belongs to whoever is learning
that not everything valuable
should be exchanged.

If you find it,
do not sell it.
Buy yourself time instead."}
{"TITLE":"The Kindness Schedule","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":28,"FONT_FAMILY":"Helvetica","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"KINDNESS SCHEDULE (WEEKLY)

MON: text someone "thinking of you" without requiring reply
TUE: let the kettle boil; drink water before caffeine

{"TITLE":"The Ladder That Ends in a Question","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":36,"FONT_FAMILY":"Palatino","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"There is a ladder behind the market

{"TITLE":"Observations on the Color of Late Afternoon","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":34,"FONT_FAMILY":"Garamond","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"Late afternoon is the color of almost.

Let the day pass through you
without collecting a toll.

{"TITLE":"The Cathedral of Vending Machines","WIDTH":700,"HEIGHT":700,"PADDING":30,"FONT_FAMILY":"Times New Roman","TITLE_COLOR":"#000000","TEXT":"At 2:00 a.m. the vending machines glow
